title: Checking a Model Against the Simulator: A Vehicle Model as a Backend, the Experiments That Tell a Wrong Parameter From a Wrong Explanation, and the Fault They Found in Our Own Robot

questions.question: What is the first thing to do when a model and a simulator disagree?
options: Fit the model's parameters to the simulator
Find which of the two the disagreement is a measurement of
Trust the simulator, which has more physics
questions.explanation: A gap says one of them is wrong about something. A fit will hide it with a number before anyone knows what it was.

questions.question: A model fitted to another model of efficiency 0.8 found:
questions.explanation: The reference had an efficiency of 0.8 and the fit recovered it with a worst gap of 0.0000 m. A fit finds a parameter when the parameter exists.

questions.question: A backend whose turn is short after a drive made turn ratios of:
questions.explanation: From rest, after driving, and after driving and a pause. A real efficiency gives the same ratio in all three; this backend did not.

questions.question: Why can no efficiency fit a context dependent backend?
options: The efficiency is one number and the behaviour depends on what came before
The fit's search is too coarse
The backend's efficiency is above one
questions.explanation: A turn that is right from rest and 30 percent short after driving cannot be matched by one constant. The best fit still left 0.013 m.

questions.question: Why was scrubbing wheels the wrong explanation for the short turn in Gazebo?
options: The turn was too slow to scrub
Scrubbing would have shortened the turn from rest too, and changing the friction changed nothing
questions.explanation: Scrubbing does not depend on what the robot did before. The turn from rest was right, and changing the friction of ground, wheels and caster moved nothing.

questions.question: What was the cause?
options: The lag of the wheel speeds
questions.explanation: The robot rocked on two wheels and a caster. With the weight over the axle the body rocked on two wheels and a caster after driving. Moving the weight behind the axle gave 0.99, 1.01 and 1.02.
